turn.student: כמה זמן אפשר לשמור ביצים במקרר?

turns.text:
המסמך שעליו אנחנו לומדים אינו מציין כמה זמן בדיוק אפשר לשמור ביצים במקרר (מעבר למסמך: בדרך כלל ביצים נשמרות במקרר כמה שבועות). 

בוא נחזור לשאלה שלנו: למה לדעתך לחם שנשאר כמה ימים בשקית מתמלא בכתמים ירוקים? אילו יצורים זעירים מתרבים עליו וגורמים לשינוי הזה [c1]?

turn.student: Magnets attract only a few materials. Iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are pulled by a magnet. Most other materials, including many metals such as aluminium, copper, gold and silver, are not attracted at all.

conceptsShown: magnets attract only a few materials

turns.text: Those are the exact words from the text. Can you explain that same idea in your own words, as if you were telling a friend why the magnet is able to separate the steel cans from the aluminium cans?

turn.student: The steel cans have iron in them so the magnet grabs them, and aluminium just isn't a magnetic metal, so those cans are left.

conceptsShown: steel cans contain iron and are pulled by the magnet
aluminium is not a magnetic metal and is not pulled

turns.text:
You correctly noted that steel cans are pulled because they contain iron, while aluminium is not magnetic and gets left behind. 

Now let's look at how a compass works. Earth itself behaves like a giant magnet [c4]. A compass contains a tiny, light needle that is actually a small magnet and can turn freely [c4]. Just like the magnets we played with earlier, where opposite poles attract, Earth's magnetic force pulls on this little needle. 

Why does a compass needle always point north?

turn.student: Because in December Australia is closer to the Sun than Europe is.

label.misconception: seasons come from distance to the Sun

turns.misconception: Thinking that summer and winter are caused by distance from the Sun (Australia is closer to the Sun in December).

assessment.misconception: Thinking that summer and winter are caused by distance from the Sun (Australia is closer to the Sun in December).

turns.text:
Let's take a quick step back to look at why summer is warmer, since distance actually isn't the reason [c4]. 

When your part of Earth is tilted towards the Sun, sunlight hits the ground more directly, just like shining a flashlight straight down on the floor instead of at a slant [c2]. 

So, when it is summer where you live, is your half of the Earth tilted towards the Sun or away from it?
